item.title: Variance-Feedback Noise in Interacting Diffusions: Shape Dynamics and Mean-Field Limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.20771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a system of $N$ attractive interacting diffusions where the variance feeds back into the noise. That is the common and idiosyncratic Brownian forcing has amplitude $\kappa(S_t^N)^q$, with $S_t^N$ the empirical variance of the system, $\kappa>0$ and $q\geq 0$. With the interaction kernel given by $K(z)=|z|^p z$, for $p\geq 0$, feedback through the empirical variance gives the system critical homogeneity at $q=(p+2)/4$. For this exponent an intrinsic time change separates the variance from the normalized centered configuration: the latter evolves autonomously on a unit sphere and, when it is not purely driven by common noise and the sphere has positive dimension, is a reversible elliptic diffusion with an explicit invariant Gibbs measure. In this case, for $p>0$, the stationary averaged dissipation gives an exact finite-particle trichotomy between consensus, recurrent excursions through arbitrarily small and large variance scales, and finite-time explosion. At critical homogeneity we also derive an autonomous unit-variance mean-field equation and its constrained free-energy dissipation identity. Across the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, we establish well-posedness and boundary classifications and prove conditional propagation of chaos on intervals where the limiting solution is unique and nonexplosive. We connect the sharp finite-particle coercivity constants to a mean-field variational problem. Finite-size It\^o corrections enlarge the universal coercive consensus region. We solve the linear model, where $p=0$, completely, including invariant laws, explosion probabilities, noncommuting limits, and an $N^{-1/2}$ transition window.
item.dc:creator: Ben Hambly, Vinh Nguyen

item.title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Tanaka

item.title: The Q-process for the general mother-dependent multitype branching process
item.description: arXiv:2610.20896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The general mother-dependent neutral mutations model is a multitype branching process describing a population evolving in discrete time, in which mutations occur among a finite set of alleles: each mutant, independently of the others, acquires an allele different from its mother's, according to a prescribed distribution. We study the associated mutant and clone-mutant chains conditioned on extinction in the distant future, that is, their $Q$-processes, and we give an explicit description of their laws in the (sub)critical and in the supercritical regimes alike. Even under this conditioning, the clone-mutant process associated with the mother-dependent neutral mutations model is obtained from the corresponding infinite-alleles BGW process (studied in Bertoin (2010) and Blancas and Rivero (2018)) by an independent multinomial colouring with specific parameters. We also obtain the spine decomposition of the multitype mutant chain, from which we derive a Kesten--Stigum theorem in the supercritical regime and a genealogical construction of the Q-process in the (sub)critical one.
item.dc:creator: Airam Blancas, Mar\'ia Clara Fittipaldi, Sara\'i Hern\'andez-Torres

item.title: Infinite-variation L\'evy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
item.description: arXiv:2610.20916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every real L\'evy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a L\'evy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Gonz\'alez C\'azares, David Kramer-Bang, Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c

item.title: $q_x$-Bass Martingales: Optimality, Existence and Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.20920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the class of $q_x$-Bass martingales, extending the notion of $q$-Bass martingales. These are martingale couplings with prescribed marginals whose transition kernels are closest to a given family of reference kernels $(q_x)_{x \in \mathbb R^d}$ in the sense of a suitable weak optimal transport problem. We show that $q_x$-Bass martingales are optimizers of this problem and establish a strong duality result. Building on this duality, we introduce an algorithm for their computation and, under compactness assumptions on the prescribed marginals, prove its convergence, thereby establishing existence. We then specialize to one-dimensional marginals and show that the algorithm reduces to a fixed-point iteration.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Marini

item.title: Competitive displacement in the grass-bushes-trees process on a scale-free network
item.description: arXiv:2610.20984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The grass-bushes-trees process is a two-type contact process in which the types face asymmetric birth mechanisms. Vertices of a graph can either be occupied by a tree, occupied by a bush, or empty (containing grass). The trees die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $\lambda_{\mathcal T}$ on any neighbouring vertex (possibly taking the place of a bush). Bushes die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $\lambda_{\mathcal B}$ on any empty neighbouring vertex; in particular, they are forbidden from taking the place of trees. We study this process on a power law random graph, namely the erased configuration model. We study which graph parameters lead to the possibility of coexistence versus the necessity of competitive displacement, i.e. joint metastability or fast extinction of the bushes.
item.dc:creator: John Fernley, Daniel Valesin

item.title: Exact Endpoint Asymptotics and Almost-Sure Limits for Uniform Empirical Measures in Two Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the empirical measure of the first $n$ points of one infinite sequence of independent uniform samples in the unit square, we identify the leading constant in the bounded-Lipschitz distance to area measure, equivalently in $W_1$, both in expectation and almost surely along all sample sizes. The constant is $c_*=\kappa_1/(2\sqrt\pi)\in(0,1/4]$, where $\kappa_1$ is the linear-growth Gaussian variational constant of Armegioiu--Goldman--Grotto--Trevisan. This answers the two-dimensional bounded-Lipschitz convergence question posed by Yukich in 1989. We give the complete endpoint argument, square--torus comparison, empirical reduction, and full-sequence probability argument.
item.dc:creator: Weitao Huang, Yichen Wu, Renzhen Wang, Deyu Meng

item.title: Gaps between roots in ballistic deposition on a strip: linear variance, Gaussian limits and a Poisson regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.21094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mansour, Rastegar and Roitershtein studied the roots of ballistic deposition on a cyclic strip of $K$ sites, namely the sites that receive a particle at height one, and the number $D_{i,K}$ of pairs of consecutive roots at distance $i+1$. They computed the first two moments of $D_{i,K}$ for $i\le7$. They conjectured that for every $i$ the mean and the variance are exactly linear in $K$, that $D_{i,K}$ satisfies a central limit theorem, and that the standardized vector $(D_{i,K})_{i\ge1}$ converges to a Gaussian process. We prove these conjectures. The key observation is that the roots are exactly the valleys of a uniformly random circular arrangement, so that $D_{i,K}$ counts occurrences of a family of consecutive patterns. We determine sizes from which the moments are exactly linear, which cannot be lowered in any case we checked, and give closed forms for the mean and variance constants and for the limiting covariance. We also prove a Wasserstein bound of order $(\mathbb{E} D_{i,K})^{-1/2}$ that is uniform in $i$, and a local limit theorem. Finally we describe the limit completely when $i$ grows with $K$: it is degenerate, Poisson or Gaussian according as $\mathbb{E} D_{i,K}$ tends to zero, to a positive constant, or to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Matijasevick

item.title: Enhanced Dissipation under Variable Growth: Stochastic $p(x)$-Laplace Equations with Transport Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.21242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study dissipation enhancement for stochastic $p(x)$-Laplace equations with divergence-free transport noise on $\mathbb T^d$, $d\ge2$. Under log-H\"older continuity and degenerate subcritical growth, we establish global variational well-posedness and an exact energy identity. For every prescribed positive coefficient, suitable transport noise yields averaged algebraic decay uniformly on bounded zero-mean $L^2$ balls. The noise is independent of the individual initial datum. This uniform enhancement holds despite the absence of homogeneous scaling and the two flux growth regimes associated with the variable exponent. We also identify $p^+$ as the optimal exponent for uniform modular coercivity near zero and obtain a strict averaged comparison with the unperturbed evolution at any prescribed time $T\ge1$ on initial-data shells with bounded gradient modular. For each prescribed decay rate and finite moment order, deterministic stepwise Fourier profiles with fixed intensity and increasing frequency range give exponential decay of the $L^2$ norm in mean square and almost surely. The absolute random prefactors have uniformly bounded moments of the prescribed order throughout the initial-data ball.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwei Zhang, Juntao Wu, Shang Wu

item.title: Small time asymptotics for kinetic SDEs with singular drift
item.description: arXiv:2610.21396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study small-time asymptotics for kinetic stochastic differential equations with singular drifts in kinetic Kato classes. We establish a small-time large deviation principle and prove a pointwise Varadhan-type asymptotic for the associated transition density.
item.dc:creator: Chongyang Ren, Saisai Yang, Tusheng Zhang

item.title: Half-space last passage percolation with inhomogeneous first row
item.description: arXiv:2610.21413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider exponential last passage percolation in half-space with a deterministic first row. This model corresponds to a version of TASEP in half-space in which particles enter at the origin and are restricted by a moving wall. We determine the possible limiting distributions of rescaled last passage times depending on the boundary strength and the choice of the wall. As key inputs to our analysis, we establish several results for point-to-point half-space last passage times, including upper tail bounds, weak convergence, and bounds on the probabilities that geodesics touch the diagonal for certain start and end points.
item.dc:creator: Patrik L. Ferrari, Sabrina Gernholt

item.title: A sharp survival threshold for branching Brownian motion in a self-generated resource environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.21476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study branching Brownian motion in a resource environment created by the particles themselves. Particles reproduce at rate $\beta$ times the resource nearby, resource is consumed at rate $c$ times the number of particles nearby, and each death returns resource mass $m$. Let $\theta=\beta m/c$, which represents the number of births supported by resource from one corpse, assuming perfect efficiency. We prove that the population dies out almost surely if $\theta\leq1$, even with perfect recycling $\left(\theta=1\right)$. If $\theta>1$ and the interaction kernel has finite range and is bounded below at short distances, the population survives with positive probability from every initial state with at least two particles, or with one particle and some resource. The threshold does not depend on the diffusivity, the death rate or the interaction kernel. We prove extinction for $\theta\leq 1$ by showing the total mass in the system to be a supermartingale. The proof of survival rests on two estimates: a large colony grows if it consumes its corpses with little waste, and a dense colony recycles corpses efficiently. Together these imply that a large, dense colony grows with exponentially high probability, and a standard doubling and restart argument then yields survival.
item.dc:creator: Maciej G{\l}uchowski, Georg Menz

item.title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.21757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Ciotir, Dan Goreac, Juan Li, Yufan Peng, Eduard Rotenstein

item.title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.
item.dc:creator: Arne Berrens, Volker Betz, Jan Giesselmann, Stefan Walter

item.title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
item.description: arXiv:2610.21864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falc\'on-Cort\'es, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $\xi_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $\xi>\xi_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $\xi_0\in (0,1)$, if $\xi$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $\xi = \xi_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour P\'olya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued P\'olya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.
item.dc:creator: Wilfred Armfield, C\'ecile Mailler

item.title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.21898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time. Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.
item.dc:creator: Ons Rameh

item.title: Sharp Cram\'er-type moderate deviation bounds for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.21975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with zero mean and variance $\sigma^2\in(0,\infty)$. In this paper, we establish a sharp Cram\'er-type moderate deviation for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums under a finite $p$-th absolute moment, $2<p\le3$. In particular, we show that $\mathbb{P}(M_n\ge xV_n)=2(1-\Phi(x))\{1+O(1)\beta_{n,p}(1+x)^p\}$ for $0\le x\le\beta_{n,p}^{-1/p}$, where $M_n=\max_{1\le k\le n}\sum_{j=1}^kX_j$, $V_n=(\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^2)^{1/2}$, $\beta_{n,p}=\mathbb{E}|X_1|^p/(n^{(p-2)/2}\sigma^p)$, and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. This proves a conjecture of Shao2010. More precisely, we bound the relative error by the same truncated-moment quantity as for self-normalized sums. The proof compares the maximum with the absolute sum while preserving their common denominator, through a reflected-walk representation and Fourier estimates with distribution-adapted smoothing.
item.dc:creator: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: Mixing time of the lazy and simple random walk on a randomly twisted hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2610.21976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a randomly twisted hypercube on $N$ vertices and study a simple or lazy random walk on this graph. We show that for both walks the mixing time is of order $\log N$, and the model does not exhibit cutoff. We also establish that both walks have cover time of order $N\log N$, and we show that the chromatic number of the graph diverges.
item.dc:creator: Zsuzsanna Baran, An{\dj}ela \v{S}arkovi\'c

item.title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
item.description: arXiv:2610.21986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. The first layer is the Kalman--Bucy filter, and subsequent layers satisfy linear equations once the lower layers are known. To derive these equations, we establish generalized Zakai and Kushner--Stratonovich equations for observation-dependent random variables and obtain explicit coefficient equations in arbitrary dimension. The conditional cumulant expansion also determines the expansion of the conditional characteristic function. We further obtain an explicit bound on the number of scalar variables in terms of the state dimension and expansion degree. When the observation function vanishes, the construction reduces to ODEs for unconditional cumulant coefficients. Comparisons with existing asymptotic-expansion algorithms illustrate the resulting reduction in the number of ODE variables.
item.dc:creator: Masahiro Kurisaki

item.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.22011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We first give a proof of the spatial Markov property without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set. We then prove that every $\mu$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $\mu$ is diffuse, the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $\mu$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. Finally, for diffuse $\mu$, we prove that a locally bounded stopping set revealing at most one point is attainable by a $\mu$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration at successive stopping times.
item.dc:creator: Ali Khezeli

item.title: Gamma Expansions of Level Two Large Deviation Rate Functionals for Metastable Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the diffusions $dX_t^\varepsilon=b(X_t^\varepsilon)dt+\sqrt{2\varepsilon}\sigma(X_t^\varepsilon)dB_t$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $b$ and $\sigma$ are smooth coefficients and $B_t$ is an $r$-dimensional Brownian motion, with $r\le d$. We allow nonreversible dynamics and a degenerate diffusion matrix. Let $\mathcal{I}_\varepsilon$ be the level-two large deviation rate functional of the empirical measure. Under our assumptions, including a complete metastable hierarchy described by resolvent convergence, we establish the full $\Gamma$-expansion $\mathcal{I}_\varepsilon=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathcal{J}^{(-1)}+\mathcal{J}^{(0)}+\sum_{p=1}^{\mathfrak{q}}\frac{1}{\theta_\varepsilon^{(p)}}\mathcal{J}^{(p)}$ in the sense of successive $\Gamma$-limits in the weak topology on probability measures. Here $\theta_\varepsilon^{(p)}$ are the metastable time scales, and each $\mathcal{J}^{(p)}$, $p\ge1$, is the lift of the level-two rate functional of the corresponding finite-state Markov chain. We establish the pre-metastable $\Gamma$-limits for generalized overdamped, underdamped, and third-order Langevin dynamics. For the generalized overdamped model, existing metastability results yield the full expansion under additional conditions. For the underdamped and third-order models, the full expansion remains conditional on verification of the complete metastable hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Donghyun Kim, Insuk Seo

item.title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process
item.description: arXiv:2610.22151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the cases in which the minimal eigenvalues of interchange-process Laplacians on two Specht modules can be compared up to a positive multiplicative constant, independent of the edge rates. In the comparable cases, we establish an inverse-polynomial lower bound for this constant. We conjecture that the constant can always be taken to be 2/3. We apply these ideas to the mixing times of the interchange and exclusion processes. Using the comparison method of Hermon, Kozma and Salez, we prove that our conjecture implies a conjecture of Oliveira on the mixing time of the interchange process. We also obtain unconditional mixing-time bounds for both processes.
item.dc:creator: Gil Alon

item.title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.22170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting biholomorphism. This semigroup encodes the local conformal structure of the CFT, in particular the Virasoro symmetry with central charge $<1$ for CILT. We first relate the quantized Segal's semigroup to Segal's amplitudes of annuli and recover the Virasoro generators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\geq0$) of CILT as generators of this semigroup. Compared to the real Liouville CFT, the main difficulty here is the absence of positivity, which we address through estimates for the imaginary Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos and non-self-adjoint operators. Using Segal's gluing axiom as in the real case, we differentiate the amplitude and use conformal covariance to derive the Ward identities in terms of all Virasoro operators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). We also outline the parallel theory for Boundary CILT (BCILT), concerning Segal's semigroup of semiannuli. These results provide essential tools for the conformal bootstrap program of (B)CILT, boundary BPZ equations, boundary structure constants, and the global construction of conformal blocks.
item.dc:creator: Yang Xiao, Yuxiao Xie

item.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.22180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai

item.title: An exact computer-assisted lower bound for Fisher-information convexity along the two-dimensional heat flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the sharp constant in the differential inequality \[ I(t)I''(t)\geq c\,[I'(t)]^2 \] for Fisher information along the probability-normalized heat flow on $\mathbb R^2$. The unrestricted log-convexity value $c=1$ is false in two dimensions, whereas the known square-root convexity theorem gives the universal value $c=1/2$. We construct an exact, machine-verifiable sum-of-squares certificate proving the stronger universal bound \[ c\geq \frac{231691}{250000}=0.926764. \] Together with an independent exact Fourier/Gaussian-envelope construction, this gives \[ 0.926764\leq c_*<0.94176665012062, \] where $c_*$ is the sharp constant for positive-time Gaussian convolutions of arbitrary probability measures on $\mathbb R^2$. We formulate the proof in explicit two-dimensional index notation. The lower bound follows from an exact rational polynomial identity involving a strictly positive denominator, a weighted total derivative, and eleven positive rational Gram matrices. All $491$ recorded leading principal minors are strictly positive and the complete polynomial identity has zero residual. No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption is imposed on the initial measure. The sharp value remains open.
item.dc:creator: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Xiaoyan Huo

item.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira

item.title: Crossing numbers of simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies crossing numbers of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes drawn in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ or $\mathbb S^{2d}$. We clarify and generalize a number of known results and conjectures from the graph case to higher dimensions: the crossing lemma (including the exceptional case of two-dimensional complexes drawn in dimension $4$), a generalized Harary-Hill conjecture (and evidence for it), existence of a midrange crossing constant (in a weak sense), and upper bound constructions based on stochastic geometry (related to Sylvester's problem) and the cyclic polytope. Some of our results are new even in the case of graphs: we give a simple proof of the Harary-Hill conjecture for antipodal drawings, and sharpen the threshold above which the rectilinear and spherical crossing numbers of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph behave like those of the complete graph.
item.dc:creator: Alfredo Hubard, Cheikh Saliou Ndiaye, Oriol Sol\'e-Pi

item.title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.21103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit McDiarmid's inequality, a central tool in statistical learning theory and algorithm analysis. We show that large deviations above the mean are exponentially unlikely for functions of independent random variables that are almost surely bounded above and satisfy a conditional moment assumption of order $p\in(1,2]$. When $p<2$, the result applies even when the function has infinite variance. Our proof relies on a new tensorization inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence, termed reverse KL tensorization, which may be of independent interest. Applications include concentration of the sample mean and median-of-means estimator, and one-sided uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.
item.dc:creator: Hanuka Eshima, Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Andrea Paudice

item.title: Pathwise Shrinkage and Probabilistic Calibration of the Multiplicative Half-Cauchy Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.21136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the multiplicative half-Cauchy process through its log-scale random-walk representation, establishing shrinkage, expansion, and critical regimes, almost-sure summability, local rebounds, and effective dimension. We also derive a semi-analytic calibration rule linking interpretable prior probability statements to its scale parameter.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Kulkarni

item.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Kernel-Based Heterogeneous Mean Field Games on a Continuum Type Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.21423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies a class of heterogeneous mean field games on a continuum type space, in which interactions are generated by a Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator acting on the type-indexed mean state profile. The control set is allowed to be a general closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, and the optimal feedback is characterized through the unique maximizer of the Hamiltonian. For a prescribed mean-field path, the stochastic maximum principle leads to a family of fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) indexed by the agent type. Under Lipschitz conditions and a monotonicity assumption on the reduced coefficients, the frozen FBSDE is globally well posed. We then formulate the consistency problem as a fixed-point problem for the kernel mean-field path. When the operator norm of the interaction kernel is sufficiently small, the resulting map has an invariant ball and is continuous and compact, so that Schauder's theorem yields existence of a mean field Nash equilibrium. Uniqueness follows under an aggregate monotonicity condition adapted to the kernel coupling. A linear-quadratic example illustrates how finite-rank interactions and heterogeneous risk preferences produce coupled collective modes, and yields a spectral smallness condition for existence and an explicit sufficient condition for uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Guangchen Wang, Luebo Xia

item.title: Multiplicative Path Weights in Networks: From Katz Connectivity to Mean First-Passage Times
item.description: arXiv:2610.21474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Signal dispersion, stress propagation in interbank systems, and transmission probabilities in epidemic and reliability models are all captured by studying paths on directed graphs where the path weight is defined as the product of its edge weights. Connectivity in such networks is naturally quantified by aggregating these multiplicative path weights across nodes. This paper provides a comprehensive treatise on connectivity and ranking measures based on multiplicative path weights. We demonstrate how standard all-path connectivity, such as the standard Katz centrality, can be extended beyond its classical spectral threshold. In addition, we derive closed-form expressions for connectivity based on first-hit paths and introduce a new version of Katz centrality. Furthermore, for random edge weights, we derive resolvent-based expressions for the first and second moments, alongside variance bounds, under a path-indexed coupling framework. Finite irreducible Markov chains are a subclass of the models studied, and we show that the scaled matrix of first-hit path probabilities is the probability-generating function for first-passage and return times, and that differentiation yields the classical first-passage times. Numerical examples illustrate the application of our results in a variety of settings.
item.dc:creator: Robbert van der Burg, Bernd Heidergott, Thao Le, Alessandro Zocca

item.title: A perturbation theory for Feynman-Kac models and their particle interpretations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a perturbation analysis of Feynman--Kac models, describing how local errors introduced at each step of the Feynman--Kac recursion propagate over time. Under general conditions on the potential functions and the Markov transitions, which are shown to hold for a large class of state-space models, we prove that the global error for any time horizon $T\geq 1$ is bounded by $C\,\Delta_T\log(1+\Delta_T^{-1})$, where $\Delta_T$ is the largest local error; this bound holds both for the prediction and the updated models. These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Del Moral, Mathieu Gerber

item.title: Persistence in probability for stochastic delay equations with multiplicative noise
item.dc:creator: Mark van den Bosch, John Ioannis Stavroulakis

item.title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} \pi(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $\pi$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.
item.dc:creator: Eeva Kuure, Markus Myllyoja, Aleksi Py\"or\"al\"a

item.title: Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
item.description: arXiv:2610.21777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $\beta$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $\beta\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $\beta=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.
item.dc:creator: Michele Giusfredi, Luca Avena, Paolo Politi

item.title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.21841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Fukasawa, Antoine Jacquier, Mugad Oumgari

item.title: Convergence Rates for Lasserre's Upper-Bound Hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with Gaussian Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.22030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative convergence rates for Lasserre's measure-based upper-bound hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ using the standard Gaussian measure as the reference measure. For any polynomial $f$ attaining its global infimum $f_{\min}$, we prove that the order-$r$ upper bounds satisfy $$ \lambda_r-f_{\min}=O\Big(\frac{1}{r}\Big), $$ yielding, to the best of our knowledge, the first explicit convergence rate for this hierarchy on a noncompact domain. We further show that the rate is sharp by proving an $\Omega(1/r)$ rate for $f=x^2$, while demonstrating that, without attainment of the infimum, convergence can be arbitrarily slow: for every $m\ge0$, we construct a polynomial whose upper bounds converge at rate $\Theta(r^{-1/(m+2)})$.
item.dc:creator: Sander Gribling, Igor Klep, Poornendu Kumar

item.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
item.description: arXiv:2610.22038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. At large redistribution or resetting rate, we find a delocalized phase and we compute the growth rate as well as the stationary distribution of the population of a given site. We show that reset-free growth episodes generate power-law stationary tails with site-dependent exponents. For weak resetting and redistribution, favorable sites can undergo long reset-free episodes and localize. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.
item.dc:creator: Maximilien Bernard, Giuseppe Del Vecchio Del Vecchio, Jean-Philippe Bouchaud, Pierre Le Doussal

item.title: Strong invariance principles in deterministic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22073v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that in every aperiodic, probability preserving dynamical system there is a function whose associated time series satisfies the almost sure invariance principle with rate asymptotically smaller then $\sqrt{n}$ and the almost sure weak invariance principle of Brosamler and Schatte.
item.dc:creator: Zemer Kosloff, Dalibor Volny

item.title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.22098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17\alpha/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.
item.dc:creator: Vadim E. Levit

item.title: Convexity, the spectrum of free Laplacians and geometric consequences: a free KLS bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.22109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a compactness theorem for the resolvent of free Laplacians. More precisely, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be a self-adjoint tuple admitting Lipschitz conjugate variables in the sense of Dabrowski (2014). Under the non-commutative curvature--dimension condition $CD(c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, introduced in our previous work (2026), we prove that the free Laplacian $\Delta:=\partial^*\bar\partial$ is proper, that is, has compact resolvent. Our argument is non-perturbative and uses a spectral variant of the free Bochner method based on Dabrowski's almost-commutation formulas. A further stochastic argument gives a normal unital trace-preserving embedding of $M=W^*(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ into $L(\mathbb F_2)$. Together, the compactness and embedding theorems gives several operator-algebraic consequences, including the Haagerup approximation property, the CMAP, and strong solidity. We also obtain proper proximality and bi-exactness. We finally obtain several geometric consequences. We prove a free analogue of Klartag's improved log--Lichnerowicz inequality (2023), together with rigidity in the equality case. More surprisingly, under $CD(0,\infty)$, we prove a dimension-free Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) bound in the free setting. As a consequence, we obtain a free thin-shell estimate for isotropic tuples. We conclude with further questions on spectral comparison with the canonical semicircular model.
item.dc:creator: Charles-Philippe Diez

item.title: Per-State Signatures and Mean Time-to-Failure: An Algorithm for Systems With Simultaneous Failures
item.description: arXiv:2610.22181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an algorithm that computes the structural signature and the mean time-to-failure (MTTF) of a monotone binary system at every one of its states, rather than only at the state in which all components work. It makes no assumption on the structure function and evaluates it exactly once per state, as many times as needed for the signature of the complete system alone, so computing the MTTF everywhere costs only a factor polynomial in the number of components over computing it once. As a by-product, it identifies all minimal path sets. We assume exchangeable component failure times whose survivor count is a continuous-time Markov chain. This setting admits simultaneous failures, as in the L\'evy-frailty Marshall-Olkin, binomial failure rate and lethal-shock models, where the simplifications available for single failures do not apply. We use the per-state MTTF to define threshold repair policies. We show that the per-state signature is a strictly finer decision criterion than the MTTF: signature dominance at a common failure count implies MTTF dominance, but not conversely. Under the L\'evy-frailty Marshall-Olkin model the MTTF is monotone in the state, which yields the long-run cost rate of every threshold policy in a single pass. Experiments on 22 benchmark networks with up to 30 components and 31 failure models show that the best MTTF-threshold policy has a median excess cost of 0.36% over the optimal state-based policy, and that it is never worse than the best policy that repairs after a fixed number of failures.
item.dc:creator: Guido Lagos, Sim\'on \'Avila

item.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.22238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.
item.dc:creator: Shiyuan Zhang, Xuheng Li, Qiwei Di, Quanquan Gu

item.title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Ismail Cosandal, Sennur Ulukus, Nail Akar

item.title: Dark Subspaces and Invariant Measures of Quantum Trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2409.18655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum trajectories are Markov processes describing the evolution of a quantum system subject to indirect measurements. They can be viewed as place dependent iterated function systems or the result of products of dependent and non identically distributed random matrices. In this article, we establish a complete classification of their invariant measures. The classification is done in two steps. First, we prove a Markov process on some linear subspaces called dark subspaces, defined in (Maassen, K\"ummerer 2006), admits a unique invariant measure. Second, we study the process inside the dark subspaces. Using a notion of minimal family of isometries from a reference space to dark subspaces, we prove a set of measures indexed by orbits of a unitary group is the set of ergodic measures of quantum trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoist, Cl\'ement Pellegrini, Anna Szczepanek

item.title: Scaling limits for allelic subfamilies in a mother-dependent multitype branching process
item.description: arXiv:2504.20030v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The mother-dependent neutral mutations model describes the evolution of a population across discrete generations in which every individual carries one of $d$ alleles and each mutant child acquires a type different from that of its mother, chosen uniformly at random. We consider a critical population with finite offspring variance and analyze the genealogy of the allelic subfamilies, extending the framework of Bertoin (2010) from the infinite-allele setting to finitely many alleles. We study the Markov chain that records the sizes of the allelic subfamilies of each type together with the numbers of mutants that they beget, and we give a $d$-dimensional random walk representation of it. In a regime of large initial population and rare mutations, we prove that the rescaled chain converges to a discrete-time continuous-state Markov process driven by the masses of the mutant populations; from the first allelic generation onwards its clone component is a multitype Ji\v{r}ina process whose branching mechanism is the Laplace exponent of a $d$-dimensional inverse Gaussian subordinator carried by the coordinate axes. Lifting this convergence to the genealogical level, we introduce a $d$-type tree of alleles and show that, in the scaling limit, it converges to a tree-indexed multitype Ji\v{r}ina process, described by the ranked atoms of Poisson random measures with inverse Gaussian intensity.
item.dc:creator: Airam Blancas, Maria Clara Fittipaldi, Sarai Hernandez-Torres

item.title: Expected Signature Kernels for Rough Paths
item.description: arXiv:2509.07893v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The expected signature kernel is a similarity measure of probability laws on path space and enters directly into signature maximum mean discrepancies. Building on [P. K. Friz, P. P. Hager, and N. Tapia, Forum Math. Sigma, 10 (2022), e42] and [M. Lemercier, T. Lyons, and C. Salvi, SIAM J. Numer. Anal., 64 (2026), pp. 1095-1125], we characterize the expected signature kernel of group-valued inhomogeneous L\'evy processes, aka L\'evy rough paths, as the scalar component of the solution to an extended Goursat-type system. We give an original description, first in the continuous case where the finite-dimensional system is exact. In the presence of jumps, this system is inherently infinite-dimensional; we prove its well-posedness and derive finite-dimensional truncations with explicit error control. This permits direct evaluation of the reference-dependent terms in one-sample signature-MMD tests without an auxiliary reference sample. Finally, for conditionally Gaussian martingales, conditioning the usual unbiased empirical squared signature-MMD on the sampled quadratic variations yields an unbiased statistic for the same quantity with no larger variance. We derive computable finite-grid versions and illustrate the resulting variance reduction and gain in power.
item.dc:creator: Peter K. Friz, Paul P. Hager

item.title: A central limit theorem for the range of random walk indexed by an infinite tree
item.description: arXiv:2511.17101v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We are interested in the second-order fluctuations of the size of the range of a random walk indexed by an infinite tree in ${\mathbb Z}^d$. Consider the Kesten tree with geometric offspring, we view the vertices on the left of its spine (the unique infinite path) as the past, and those on the right as the future. We show that the number of new sites in the future given its past has linear variance when $d>8$, and satisfies a central limit theorem (CLT) with Gaussian limiting distribution when $d>16$. The proof relies on the stationarity of the model under depth-first exploration, a general CLT by Dedecker and Merlev\`ede [7], a truncation technique exploiting the local independence of tree structures, and a recursion argument for moment bounds.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Bai, Yueyun Hu

item.title: Fluctuations from a random fractional averaging limit
item.description: arXiv:2512.08621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a system of multiscale stochastic differential equations whose slow component is drivenby a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H greater than 1/2. Under ergodic assumptions ensuring the applicability of the fractional averaging and fractional homogenization theorems of Hairer and Li (arXiv:1902.11251, arXiv:2109.06948), we establish a fluctuation result. The deviation of the slow motion, scaled by epsilon^{1/2-H}, from its effective, time-dependent random limit converges, as the time-separation scale epsilon tends to zero, to the solution of a stochastic differential equation driven by a fractional Brownian motion and influenced by an additional space--time Gaussian field. Since the averaging principle and the fractional homogenization hold in different modes of convergence, obtaining the required joint convergence is a delicate matter. Moreover, neither the continuity of the Ito--Lyons solution map nor the martingale method is directly applicable for our purposes, so the proof requires several innovations. To establish the fluctuation theorem, we combine cumulant methods with a residue lemma and formulate the enlarged system as a rough differential equation in a suitable space.
item.dc:creator: Xue-Mei Li, Colin Piernot, Szymon Sobczak, Kexing Ying

item.title: Random walk on the small-world network model in 3 or more dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.12056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mixing time of a simple random walk on the small-world network defined by adding edges to $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ as follows: for each pair $\{x,y\}$ we add an edge with probability $Z_n/\|x-y\|^{d}$ with $Z_n$ chosen so that the average number of added edges to every vertex is $1$. When $d\geq 3$, we show that with high probability the mixing time is of order $\log n$ and that the random walk does not exhibit cutoff.
item.dc:creator: Zsuzsanna Baran, Jonathan Hermon, An{\dj}ela \v{S}arkovi\'c, Allan Sly, Perla Sousi

item.title: Uniform Bessel bounds for magnetization crossings in finite Ising chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.06935v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a finite zero-field Ising chain, the all-up configuration and zero magnetization become equally likely at a single coupling. This crossing has recently been described as a thermal transition of the finite chain, an analogue of a first-order transition temperature, and approximated by an analytic estimate and a numerical fit. We find its asymptotics, with explicit constants, for free and for periodic ends. The coupling at the crossing grows like half the logarithm of the length of the chain, minus half the logarithm of that logarithm. So the correlation length at the crossing is a vanishing fraction of the chain. Periodic ends lower the coupling at the crossing by an amount that decays like the inverse logarithm of the length. The earlier approximations lack the doubly logarithmic term, which explains why a fit on chains of moderate length finds a slope below one half. The proofs treat the magnetization as the position of a persistent random walk and compare its central probability with a modified Bessel function, with a relative error bound that is explicit for every length. For free ends this traps the crossing in an explicit interval at every length. The proof is analytic for long chains and uses exact integer arithmetic for short ones. We also locate, for each smaller magnetization, the coupling at which it becomes as likely as full magnetization.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
item.description: arXiv:2610.13659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.
item.dc:creator: Frank van der Meulen

item.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
item.description: arXiv:2610.16339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished. The results are formalised in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Troscheit

item.title: Construction of Gross-Neveu model using Polchinski flow equation
item.description: arXiv:2403.18562v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a new method for solving the renormalization group flow equation, also known as the Polchinski equation, by formulating it as a well-posed infinite-dimensional partial differential equation on a Banach space. This yields the first direct construction of a solution of this equation via a fixed point argument, circumventing the need for perturbative or expansion-based techniques employed in earlier work. Our approach leverages recent advances in noncommutative probability theory, particularly a scale decomposition of the free fermionic field in a filtered noncommutative probability space equipped with a suitable conditional expectation. As a key application, we construct the Gross-Neveu model, a fermionic, asymptotically free, and scaling-critical quantum field theory. We rigorously establish convergence of the Schwinger functions as the cutoff is removed, and construct a random field on the noncommutative probability space of the free theory whose moments coincide with the Schwinger functions. This provides the first explicit strong coupling between the free and interacting fields for a scaling-critical quantum field theory. The method is expected to apply broadly to other critical or subcritical quantum field theories formulated in terms of bounded fields, including fermionic models such as the symplectic fermion model, as well as certain bosonic theories like the sine-Gordon model.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch

item.title: Second Maximum of a Gaussian Random Field and Exact (t-)Spacing test
item.description: arXiv:2406.18397v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce the novel concept of the second maximum of a Gaussian random field defined on a Riemannian manifold: Once the field reaches its global maximum at a point $t_1$, the second maximum is the largest value of the field away from $t_1$, after the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$ have been removed. This statistic serves as a powerful tool for characterizing the distribution of the global maximum. By employing an ad-hoc Kac-Rice formula, we derive the explicit distribution of the maximum, conditioned on the second maximum and the independent part of the Riemannian Hessian (the part of the Hessian at $t_1$ that is independent of the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$). This approach yields an exact test based on the spacing between these maxima, which we refer to as the spacing test. We investigate the applicability of this test for detecting sparse alternatives in Gaussian symmetric tensors, continuous sparse deconvolution, and two-layered neural networks with smooth rectifiers. Theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the calibration and power of the proposed procedures. More generally, we provide a framework for applying the spacing test to continuous sparse regression for any Gaussian random field on a Riemannian manifold. Furthermore, when the variance-covariance function is known only up to a scaling factor, we derive an exact Studentized version of the procedure, coined the t-spacing test. We show that this test is perfectly calibrated under the null hypothesis and exhibits high power for detecting sparse alternatives. As a corollary, we derive an exact, non-asymptotic test for the spiked tensor model without requiring prior knowledge of the noise level.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marc Aza\"is, Federico Dalmao, Yohann De Castro

item.title: Stochastic internal habit formation and optimality
item.description: arXiv:2502.05081v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Growth models with internal habit formation have been studied in various settings under the assumption of deterministic dynamics. The purpose of this paper is to explore a stochastic version of the model in Carroll et al. [1997, 2000], one the most influential on the subject. The goal is twofold: on one hand, to determine how far we can advance in the technical study of the model; on the other, to assess whether at least some of the deterministic outcomes remain valid in the stochastic setting. The resulting optimal control problem proves to be challenging, primarily due to the lack of concavity in the objective function. This feature is present in the model even in the deterministic case (see, e.g., Bambi and Gozzi [2020]). We develop an approach based on Dynamic Programming to establish several useful results, including the regularity of the solution to the corresponding HJB equation and a verification theorem. There results lay the groundwork for studying the model optimal paths and comparing them with the deterministic case.
item.dc:creator: Michele Aleandri, Alessandro Bondi, Fausto Gozzi

item.title: Optimal Transport on Lie Group Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2508.09377v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In its most general form, the optimal problem is an infinite-dimensional optimization problem, yet certain notable instances admit closed-form solutions. We identify the common source of this tractability as \textit{symmetry} and formalize it using Lie group theory. Fixing a Lie group action and a reference distribution, we study optimal transport between measures in the same orbit. For such pairs of measures, restricting the Monge problem to transport maps induced by the group action yields the Lie group orbit transport problem, an optimization over the stabilizer of the reference law that provides an upper bound on the Monge problem. Under suitable regularity conditions, a feasible group-induced map satisfying a $c$-convex first-order certificate attains this bound, solves the original Monge problem, and induces an optimal Kantorovich plan. For the quadratic cost, we establish a structural criterion based on a global Cartan decomposition. Exploiting the nonuniqueness of orbit representations, the criterion constructs an optimal map through a path of group transformations with self-adjoint derivatives. Once verified for an action and reference law, it applies to every pair of orbit measures with finite second moments. For affine-induced actions, Cartan structure on the linear image suffices, and the means and covariance operators determine the optimal map and value explicitly. The framework recovers classical elliptical transport formulas and yields closed-form solutions on congruence orbits generated by absolutely continuous, spectrally invariant reference laws, including Wishart, inverse-Wishart, and matrix beta type~II families with fixed shape parameters. It also recovers the common-copula optimal coupling for multivariate normal sinh-arcsinh laws with unit tailweight parameters sharing a Gaussian copula, and evaluates the optimal transport value in closed form.

item.title: Quality control in sublinear time: a case study via random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2508.16531v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many algorithms are designed to work well on average over inputs. But when such an algorithm is run on an arbitrary input, the question arises: Can we trust the algorithm on this input? This question is especially relevant in network science, where algorithms for theoretical random graph models are often applied to individual real-world networks. We identify a new class of algorithmic problems addressing this, which we call "Quality Control Problems." These problems are specified by a "quality function" $\rho$ and a distribution $D$ such that, with high probability, a sample drawn from $D$ is "high quality," meaning its $\rho$-value is near $1$. The goal is to accept most inputs $x \sim D$ and reject potentially adversarially generated inputs $x$ with $\rho(x)$ far from $1$. In this work, we consider the sublinear version of the quality control problem, where $D \in \Delta(\{0,1\}^N)$ and the goal is to solve the $(D,\rho)$-quality problem with $o(N)$ queries and time. As a case study, we consider random graphs, i.e., $D = G_{n,p}$ (and $N = \binom{n}2$), and the $k$-clique count function $\rho_k := C_k(G)/\mathbb{E}_{G' \sim G_{n,p}}[C_k(G')]$, where $C_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-cliques in $G$. In suitable parameter ranges, worst-case approximate $k$-clique counting requires $p^{-\Omega(k^2)}$ queries. In contrast, we show that the quality control problem for $G_{n,p}$ (with $n\geq p^{-ck}$ for some constant $c$) with respect to $\rho_k$ can be tested with $p^{-O(k)}$ queries and time, showing quality control is provably superpolynomially more efficient in this setting. More generally, for a motif $H$ of maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, we show that the corresponding quality control problem can be solved with $p^{-O(\Delta(H))}$ queries and running time.

item.title: An inductive approach to stochastic estimates for the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation with correlated coefficient fields
item.description: arXiv:2509.11309v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an inductive approach to obtain stochastic estimates for singular SPDEs when the coefficient field is correlated with the driving noise. We implement our method, in the whole space, on the example of the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation. Our approach is based on (infinite-dimensional) integration by parts with respect to Wick products of Gaussian random variables (more precisely, mollifications of space-time white noise) together with an inductive scheme over the moment's exponent.

item.title: Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics (after Y. Deng, Z. Hani, and X. Ma)
item.description: arXiv:2602.04407v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider a microscopic system of $N$ hard spheres that are initially independent (modulo the exclusion condition on particle positions) and identically distributed in $\mathbb{R}^3$. When the number $N$ of particles goes to infinity and the diameter $\varepsilon$ of the particles goes to zero, and under the weak density assumption $N\varepsilon^2=1$, it has been known since the work of Lanford that the empirical measure for the particles converges to the solution of the Boltzmann equation in a short time interval. In particular, the particles remain dynamically independent, in this limit and in the short time interval where the correlations induced by their collisions remain under control. In a recent work, Y. Deng, Z. Hani and X. Ma successfully obtained the same convergence result in arbitrary large time; more precisely, the convergence result holds for any time interval on which the Boltzmann equation has a regular solution. In this note, we explain a few elements of their proof.

item.title: Ergodicity for a Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio model of turbulent flow
item.description: arXiv:2603.06182v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents a mathematical analysis of a one-dimensional model of turbulence based on a stochastic generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio (gCLMG) equation. We focus on the specific case where the nonlinearity in the equation allows the existence of the anomalous enstrophy cascade, which is an inviscid conserved quantity, and some effective energy estimates for mathematical analysis. The existence of an invariant measure in the attractor is proved via the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov argument. The uniqueness of the measure and exponential mixing are proved under a sufficiently large viscosity condition, in which the nonlocal structure of the nonlinear term plays a prominent role. The construction of this invariant measure is the first step towards a theoretical understanding of turbulent phenomena that cause anomalous cascades in the zero viscous limit, viewed from the dynamical systems theory.

item.title: Efficient sampling of the unlabeled structure of uniform random mappings and surjections
item.description: arXiv:2605.24068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article deals with the sampling and statistics of uniform random mappings and surjections from $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. More precisely, we focus on statistics that are invariant under relabeling of the domain and codomain. The structure of a mapping or surjection up to relabeling is captured by a compact representation called its profile. The profile records, for each occurring preimage size, the number of preimages of that size. We provide a complete set of algorithms that directly sample the profiles of uniform random mappings and surjections, covering the full parameter space. Their expected running times match the expected length of their outputs up to logarithmic factors. It is important to note that we make no assumption about the relationship between $n$ and $k$; in particular, we do not assume that $n/k$ is constant. All our guarantees are uniform in $n$ and $k$. Achieving this uniformity substantially complicates the analysis. Our algorithms are based on exact-size Boltzmann samplers, which we accelerate by optimizing the cost of each sampling round and increasing the acceptance probability. As spin-off results, we answer, up to a logarithmic factor, an open question of Devroye and Los~25 on sampling profiles of random mappings when $n>k\log k$, and obtain a sampler for uniform random surjections with expected running time $O(n\log k)$, valid across the full parameter space.

item.title: Dynamic models with $p$ parameters are identified by $2p+1$ random features
item.description: arXiv:2607.16035v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A foundational principle in nonlinear dynamics is that the structure of a dynamical system can be recovered from a small number of generic measurements or coordinates. We develop an analogous principle for the identification of dynamic models for time series \textit{with noise}, which builds on previous identification results for noiseless dynamical systems. The noise is allowed to be non-iid, non-Gaussian, and dependent on the state. Our results cover noisily observed differential equations and discrete-time dynamical systems, as well as stochastic models with process noise. We illustrate the utility of this identification principle using a Lorenz-63 model and a H\'{e}non map model, both with observational noise.
